summary: AE + SE walked Solstice through Redwood's open-model scouting flow, compatibility matrix, and bench interpretation. Customer cares about 95ms median latency for chat-ish prompts, strict PHI handling, and preferring reserved capacity if prices amortize. Agreed to share bench sheet and kick off a short dedicated POC after security check.
topics: bench selection and interpreting token cost vs latency
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-11 15:00 PST — Duration 38m; Recording: yes; Location: Zoom; Notes: deck link shared (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/solstice-catalog-demo)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving the time today. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Ravi, our solutions engineer. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Alicia Gomez: Hi Maya, Alicia here, CTO.
[00:15] Mark Tsu: Mark, ML Eng.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Priya, security.
[00:20] David Lin: David, product.
[00:23] Ravi Patel: Hi all — Ravi, SE. We'll try to keep this focused on the catalog scouting flow and the bench interpretation section.

[00:40] Maya Chen: Super. Agenda — quick discovery to align on SLOs, then walkthrough of the model catalog UI, how we shortlist open models, where bench numbers live, and then the compatibility matrix — K-V cache, quant bits, kernel mapping. We'll stop for Qs.

[01:05] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. Our main driver: we want reduced hallucination on clinical notes and latency around 95 to 120ms for short chat sequences, cost is important but we can't compromise PHI handling. We expect SOC2 or similar and KMS integration.

[01:32] Maya Chen: Great, that's helpful. Quick question on traffic — are you expecting bursty spikes with many short requests or more steady streams?
[01:40] Mark Tsu: Mostly short bursts — UI chat, front-line staff hitting a UI. Concurrency could be hundreds during shift changes, but each session is usually 4–8 tokens per turn plus longer context sometimes.

[01:58] Ravi Patel: Ok makes sense. That profile tends to favor lower-latency kernels and prefix cache to reduce repeated compute for history. We'll show where those settings live.

[02:10] David Lin: Also — we may be restricted on cross-region data movement. We need to keep logs in the same jurisdiction.

[02:18] Priya Rao: And our compliance team will need a security walkthrough — KMS, audit logs, SSO — SAML specifically.

[02:26] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll call out our Private deployment and dedicated options for that.

[02:40] [Screen share begins — Redwood Console, Model Catalog]

[02:45] Ravi Patel: Alright, opening the catalog. Top-left you can filter by use-case, say 'conversational' or 'instruction', and by quantization. We'll start with open-models tagged for low-latency. See these three candidates — m-open-8q and m-open-7b-int8 and a 13b float baseline.

[03:20] Mark Tsu: Quick ask — how do you compute those latency numbers? Are they medians over the whole dataset or specific to seq len?

[03:28] Ravi Patel: Good question. Benchmarks are measured by sequence length slices — medians reported on the typical length bucket for a given workload. For UI chat we tag the 32-token bucket; you can view raw distributions in the bench csv that we attach. Note there is a device-specific kernel mapping that affects tail latency.

[03:52] Maya Chen: I'm going to pull up the compatibility matrix. This is where we show kernel maturity and quant friendliness per model. The matrix will say 'green' for native int8 flow, 'yellow' if it's supported but slower, and 'red' if we don't recommend.

[04:12] Priya Rao: Is that mapping static? Like if a new kernel lands, do you re-run?

[04:18] Ravi Patel: We rerun tests when we onboard a kernel or a model patch. There's an automated job but we also do manual QA for new open-model variants.

[04:35] [00:04:38] Maya Chen: You'll also see a column for KV cache compatibility — some quant flows don't support efficient KV caching which can blow per-token cost for multi-turn.

[04:54] Mark Tsu: Can you elaborate — you mean the K-V as in key-value cache? We sometimes see 'K-V cash' in other transcripts ha — but yeah, does int8 affect the cache?

[05:04] Ravi Patel: Yes, KV cache. Some lower-precision runtimes store cached tensors differently which can increase memory pressure and change batching behavior. For session-heavy chat, we usually recommend models with full KV cache support in the quant path.

[05:20] Maya Chen: I'll pull a bench sample. Here's a bench for three candidate models against our 32-token synthetic prompts. Column A: median latency; B: 95th percentile; C: tokens/sec; D: cost per 1k tokens under a given infra estimate.

[05:45] David Lin: That cost column — is it specific to hosted Redwood or indicative of dedicated amortized GPU cost?

[05:52] Ravi Patel: The sheet has both. We present 'hosted unit cost' and a 'dedicated amortized per-token' assuming your committed pool size and expected utilization. For Solstice, if you commit to reserved capacity the per-token falls significantly, but there's a minimum commit.

[06:10] Alicia Gomez: What's the break-even point roughly? At what monthly throughput does dedicated become cheaper?

[06:16] Ravi Patel: Roughly, for our baseline assumptions, around 20M tokens per month for the 8q model on a T4-equivalent pool; for 13b float it might be 8–10M due to higher GPU hours. We'll give tuned numbers in the spreadsheet for your exact workload.

[06:35] Priya Rao: From security side — you mentioned Private with customer-managed control plane. Does the private offering support bringing your own KMS/HSM?

[06:44] Maya Chen: Yes — Private supports KMS integrations and can use customer HSMs for key wrapping. We also provide audit logs accessible by your SIEM. We have SOC 2 Type II attestation; we can share the report after an NDA.

[06:58] Priya Rao: Please send the SOC2 and encryption docs. Also, what about data residency?

[07:04] Maya Chen: You can pin deployments to regions; for Private you can deploy entirely in your VPC or on-prem.

[07:12] Mark Tsu: Back to bench interpret — how do we account for RLHF/regenerated responses affecting latency? Like if the model does multiple decode passes for safety checks, does bench simulate that?

[07:22] Ravi Patel: Bench is configurable. We can simulate decode-time safety filters by adding extra decoding steps or scorer calls; those will factor into latency and cost. For your clinical use-case we recommend adding a reranker pass in the bench to surface regression in quality vs cost.

[07:40] [07:40] David Lin: I saw a column called 'fallback compatibility' — what is that?

[07:46] Maya Chen: That's our routing playbook mapping — if a model isn't available we can automatically route to a lower-cost variant or a hosted fallback with different latency characteristics. You can set policies by SLO or cost thresholds.

[08:02] Mark Tsu: Any examples of production fallback? Like degrade to 7b-int8 for non-sensitive calls?

[08:09] Ravi Patel: Exactly. You can tag endpoints with data-sensitivity levels and routing rules so PHI routes to Private Dedicated pools and public or less sensitive goes to hosted cheaper variants.

[08:22] Priya Rao: Is the routing deterministic? We need to be able to audit decisions for compliance.

[08:28] Maya Chen: Routing decisions are logged with trace IDs and the route policy. Those logs are retained per your retention settings and are available to your security team.

[08:40] [Screen — Compatibility matrix detail]

[08:45] Ravi Patel: Here's a slightly tricky note — there's models that are fast on A100 kernels but slower on T4 due to attention kernel choices. That's why we show kernel mapping per model and per device. If you're deploying private, we recommend matching your committed hardware to the kernels we certify.

[09:06] Alicia Gomez: We're likely to start with a smaller GPU type for cost reasons. How painful is the re-tune if we later change hardware?

[09:14] Ravi Patel: There's a re-compilation step. Our platform will re-select kernels and we'll recommend quant profiles. Usually it's a quick re-run but tail-latency surprises are possible; we can help with a short bench sprint to validate.

[09:30] Mark Tsu: On the catalog, can we lock model versions so we don't get surprises when a community model updates?

[09:36] Maya Chen: Yes — you can pin model versions and use Redwood rollouts for canarying. We also show model provenance and last-updated notes, but you control which exact build you serve.

[09:50] David Lin: For evaluation of hallucination, do you provide any quality signals integrated with the bench?

[09:57] Ravi Patel: We have a 'quality' tab in the bench where you can run your eval prompts — redwood-evals — and collect metrics like F1, hallucination rate, and answer-match. Those can be tied to alerts so rollouts fail if quality drops.

[10:18] Priya Rao: Any PII scrubbing integrations if we ingest logs for monitoring?

[10:24] Maya Chen: We offer server-side PII redaction rules for hosted; for Private you can run our redactor in your VPC or bring your own.

[10:35] [10:35] Mark Tsu: Does the console expose live per-route token costs?

[10:39] Ravi Patel: Yes — Console shows per-route cost, per-model, per-token breakdown with traceable requests. That's useful for debugging where cost spikes happen.

[10:48] David Lin: Let's talk success criteria: to go into a POC we need to see median latency <120ms for 32-token UI prompts at 95%ile under our concurrency profile, and an audit of security controls.

[10:59] Maya Chen: Makes sense. We'll aim to get you a dedicated pool bench and a security packet.

[11:10] [11:10] Alicia Gomez: On the cost side — provide an example amortization table for reserved capacity including burst. We want to show execs the projected monthly run-rate.

[11:20] Maya Chen: We'll include a few amortization scenarios.

[11:25] Mark Tsu: A couple of nitty-gritty items — do you support mixed precision quant (e.g., 4-bit for weights but 8-bit for activations)?

[11:33] Ravi Patel: Some of our runtime paths support hybrid quant; the compatibility matrix flags that. For production we guide to the profiles we've validated.

[11:44] Priya Rao: Re: logs — how long are audit logs retained by default?

[11:49] Maya Chen: Default hosted retention is 90 days; on Private you set retention. We can also push to your SIEM in real-time.

[11:58] [12:00] David Lin: Okay let's run a quick hands-on — can you show creating a shortlist and kicking off a bench?

[12:05] Ravi Patel: Yep. In the catalog you select candidates and click 'Run bench'. Choose your prompt set — I'll pick the 'conversational-32' you can upload custom prompts. Set infra target — I'll choose a 'dedicated-small' template and set concurrency profile.

[12:28] [12:28] Ravi Patel: Kicking off — job queued. You get a job id and we'll stream results as they come. The bench runner shows per-step breakdown: tokenization, forward pass, KV write, decode.

[12:45] Mark Tsu: For our real prompts could you run a reranker pass as part of bench?

[12:50] Ravi Patel: Absolutely — you can add a scoring function and we support multi-stage benches.

[13:00] [13:00] Maya Chen: A small note on accuracy of benches — synthetic benches are good as an early filter but we recommend at least one run on customer prompt set in a POC to catch data-specific regressions.

[13:12] Alicia Gomez: That's what we want to see in the POC.

[13:15] [13:15] Priya Rao: Anything to call out re: logging PHI in the bench? We don't want actual PHI leaving our environment.

[13:22] Ravi Patel: For Private/On-prem benches you can run the bench within your VPC so PHI never leaves. For hosted benches we recommend anonymized or synthetic data.

[13:35] Maya Chen: Quick Q — are there cost guardrails to prevent runaway bills during POC?

[13:41] Ravi Patel: Yes — quotas, per-route caps, and alerts. You can set hard limits on tokens per day and auto-throttle.

[13:50] David Lin: Can Redwood integrate with our billing or tag requests for internal chargeback?

[13:56] Maya Chen: We support tagging and export of cost reports; you can ingest into your internal chargeback system.

[14:05] [14:05] Mark Tsu: A potential concern: if we choose a model with 'yellow' compatibility in the matrix, how much engineering lift should we expect to get it production-ready?

[14:15] Ravi Patel: Yellow usually means supported but requires kernel updates or a tweak in quant profile. Typically 1–2 engineer-weeks depending on model size; we can staff an onboarding SE to help.

[14:30] Priya Rao: For the POC, will Redwood help with SOC-like evidence, or do we need a separate audit?

[14:36] Maya Chen: We can provide artifact packs (config, logs, controls mappings) and coordinate with our compliance team. For formal audits we can coordinate a bridge letter or share reports under NDA.

[14:50] [14:50] David Lin: Great. Any limitations on function-calling or structured outputs with quantized models?

[14:57] Ravi Patel: Function-calling works — but for some extreme low-bit paths we recommend validating structured output as part of the bench. The path can introduce slight differences that affect parsing.

[15:12] Maya Chen: We're approaching 15 minutes in — want to surface some sample next steps. We'll send the bench spreadsheet and an initial shortlist (Maya). Ravi will prepare a short private-deploy checklist for network and infra. Priya will share the security questionnaire and regulatory constraints. Then we'll propose POC windows.

[15:30] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. If you can include an amortization table that'd help my leadership.

[15:36] Maya Chen: Will do.

[15:40] [15:40] Mark Tsu: One last techie: do you expose kernel-level perf counters so we can do deep dives?

[15:45] Ravi Patel: We expose trace hooks and perf counters in dedicated and private modes; hosted gives aggregated metrics for security reasons.

[15:55] Priya Rao: Ok I'm mostly satisfied on controls as long as the SOC2 packet and KMS info arrive.

[16:00] Maya Chen: We'll attach those in the follow-up.

[16:05] David Lin: Thanks everyone — that's helpful.

[16:10] Maya Chen: Quick recap: Redwood to share deck, bench spreadsheet, amortization scenarios, SOC2 and KMS docs (Maya). Ravi to send private deployment network checklist and bench run template (Ravi). Solstice to send real prompt set + SLOs and internal security questionnaire (Mark/Priya). Aim to have due items by next week and then kickoff a 1-week dedicated POC.

[16:30] Alicia Gomez: Thanks all.

[16:33] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up in email and post the bench sheet link.

[16:38] [Call ends]

End transcript. Notes: minor transcription glitches — 'K-V cash' transcription shows up in a few spots; some product names miscapitalized. Deck link and bench csv referenced.
